Main findings: Deficit in the task-related activation in the striatum and its frontal motor area projections
Lower loss of glucose uptake than of D 2 receptor levels (2.3 % vs. 6.3 % per year)
Lower caudate metabolism in patients with pre-HD converted to HD than in patients with pre-HD not converted (5-years follow-up)
Decrease in D 2 receptors in the striatum but not in extrastriatal areas. Correlation between striatum D 2 receptor loss and motor symptoms
Increase in activation of microglia in striatal and cortical areas in pre-HD patients. Correlation between increased TSPO in associative striatum and cognitive dysfunction
Decrease in CB 1 receptors in the cerebrum and cerebellum (grey matter) and brainstem
